findings.highlight: my mind that cannot mourn enough is still burning too
findings.evidenceJa: 悔やみきれない心は燻ったままだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s heart continues to smolder with regret that cannot be exhausted.
findings.explanation: Mourn shifts self-reproach over preventable harm toward grief for a death and weakens the ethical pressure driving him.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka said nobody died
findings.evidenceJa: 死傷者はいないと遠坂は言っていた
findings.governingReading: Rin reported that there were no dead or injured casualties, which Shirou immediately treats as only the surface account.
findings.explanation: Nobody died removes the claim about injury and weakens the paradox between the official report and lasting harm.

findings.highlight: Long-term physical disabilities
findings.evidenceJa: 長期に渡る身体不良
findings.governingReading: Shirou anticipates prolonged bodily ill health or dysfunction.
findings.explanation: Disabilities intensifies an anticipated period of poor condition into lasting disability without support.

findings.highlight: mental damage from lack of oxygen
findings.evidenceJa: 酸欠による記憶障害
findings.governingReading: Shirou specifically anticipates memory impairment caused by oxygen deprivation.
findings.explanation: Mental damage broadens a concrete cognitive consequence into an undefined and more sweeping injury.

findings.highlight: students that had their skin melted
findings.evidenceJa: 肌に重傷を負った生徒
findings.governingReading: Some students sustained serious injuries to their skin.
findings.explanation: The mature branch invents melting as the mechanism of injury.

findings.highlight: It’s ridiculous for my mind to grumble about such a thing.
findings.evidenceJa: 体が弱って、心までそんな世迷い事をクチにする
findings.governingReading: Shirou is angry that because his body has weakened, even his heart has begun voicing such nonsense.
findings.explanation: The English removes the causal link between bodily weakness and the momentary wish to erase what happened.

findings.highlight: I should do so until the point of my death
findings.evidenceJa: 死の淵まで、その
findings.governingReading: The thought reaches “to the brink of death, that—” and deliberately cuts off as Shirou wakes.
findings.explanation: The English completes the broken thought into a maxim about continuing until his own death, adding a proposition the source withholds.

findings.highlight: A sharp pain runs through my left arm as if there’s a crack in my bone.
findings.evidenceJa: 亀裂でも入ったかのように、左肩が痛んだ
findings.governingReading: Shirou’s left shoulder hurts as though a crack has formed.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the pain to the arm and supplies bone as a diagnosed substrate that the comparison leaves unstated.

findings.highlight: my body was so weak
findings.evidenceJa: 体中がドロドロで
findings.governingReading: After Berserker’s strike, Shirou felt his whole body reduced to a viscous, mush-like state.
findings.explanation: Weak removes the grotesque bodily dissolution image used to distinguish that prior injury.

findings.highlight: I cannot ignore what you have just said.
findings.evidenceJa: 今の発言は聞き捨てなりません
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese begins with Saber asking what Shirou just said he would do; the preceding declaration is commented out.
findings.explanation: One Classic voice-disabled branch restores superseded dialogue and makes Saber’s rebuke longer than the active source.

findings.highlight: find Shinji before the day is over
findings.evidenceJa: 今日中に慎二を捕まえる
findings.governingReading: Shirou insists they will capture Shinji before the day ends.
findings.explanation: Find reduces a concrete plan to seize and stop Shinji into locating him.

findings.highlight: Saber shuts her mouth.
findings.evidenceJa: それきりセイバーは口を閉ざした
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese ends on Saber’s reluctant statement that she can only obey; the narration that she falls silent is commented out.
findings.explanation: The Classic branch restores a deleted narrative beat and renders it in blunt, character-damaging English.

findings.highlight: she’ll make me realize how stupid I am
findings.evidenceJa: 小さくなるっていうか
findings.governingReading: Rin’s reaction not only makes Shirou recognize his stupidity but leaves him figuratively shrinking with embarrassment.
findings.explanation: The English omits his deflated physical-social reaction and leaves only the abstract realization.

findings.highlight: grave face
findings.evidenceJa: 気の乗らない顔
findings.governingReading: Rin asks why Shirou looks reluctant or unenthusiastic about their apparent advantage.
findings.explanation: Grave changes hesitation about the plan into generalized solemnity.

findings.highlight: I feel like we shouldn’t even challenge her
findings.evidenceJa: 挑んではいけない相手のような気さえする
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese ends after Shirou says they cannot be optimistic about Rider’s trump card; the stronger thought that she may be an opponent they must not challenge is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores a superseded conclusion and strengthens Shirou’s tactical judgment.

findings.highlight: close to the magic you use
findings.evidenceJa: 凛の使う魔術に近い
findings.governingReading: Saber says the phenomenon is categorically close to the Magecraft Rin uses.
findings.explanation: Generic magic erases the local technical distinction that the following exchange explicitly tests against true Magic.

findings.highlight: Your magic resistance is godly
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーの対魔術は神業じゃない
findings.governingReading: Rin says Saber’s resistance to Magecraft is no ordinary feat, not literally a divine property.
findings.explanation: Godly promotes an idiom of extraordinary ability into a metaphysical quality within an already technical explanation.

findings.highlight: No magic in the present day can hurt you.
findings.evidenceJa: 現代の魔術じゃまず貴女に傷を負わせる事はできない
findings.governingReading: Ordinary modern Magecraft can scarcely be expected to wound Saber.
findings.explanation: No makes the qualified practical immunity absolute and again calls Magecraft magic.

findings.highlight: Divine mysteries are nullified by even stronger ones.
findings.evidenceJa: 神秘はより強い神秘の前に無効化される
findings.governingReading: Mystery is nullified before a stronger Mystery.
findings.explanation: Divine adds a property absent from the rule and destabilizes Fate’s technical category of Mystery.

findings.highlight: are you saying Rider is a magus
findings.evidenceJa: 魔法使い
findings.governingReading: Rin hears Magic and asks whether Saber is saying Rider is a true Magician.
findings.explanation: Magus collapses 魔法使い into the distinct practitioner of 魔術, destroying the very contrast Rin is reacting to.

findings.highlight: If there is a magus, it could only be Caster.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔法使いがいるとすれば、それはキャスターだけ
findings.governingReading: Saber replies that if any class were a Magician, it would only be Caster.
findings.explanation: Magus repeats the category collapse and makes Saber’s reply false on its own terms, since the conversation already distinguishes ordinary magi.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka gives a relieved sigh
findings.evidenceJa: ほっと胸をなで下ろす遠坂
findings.governingReading: Rin visibly strokes her chest in relief at Saber’s answer.
findings.explanation: The English replaces a concrete gesture with a generic sigh and changes the scene’s physical characterization.

findings.highlight: only sorcery can go through it
findings.evidenceJa: 魔法でなければ通らない
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether only true Magic can penetrate Saber’s armor.
findings.explanation: Sorcery uses an unstable English category in the middle of a distinction between Magic and Magecraft.

findings.highlight: close to sorcery
findings.evidenceJa: 魔法に近い
findings.governingReading: Saber describes Gae Bolg as a curse close to true Magic.
findings.explanation: Sorcery again blurs the exceptional category being used to characterize the curse.

findings.highlight: you are misinterpreting that Saber can be only hurt using sorcery
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーは魔法じゃないと傷つかない、と勘違いしてる
findings.governingReading: Rin asks whether Shirou mistakenly thinks Saber cannot be harmed except by true Magic.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and leaves the condition’s scope hard to parse.

findings.highlight: attacking using magic from a distance
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術っていう飛び道具
findings.governingReading: The remaining option is a ranged projectile in the form of Magecraft.
findings.explanation: Magic removes the technical category whose interaction with Magic Resistance is being explained.

findings.highlight: direct intervention like shooting an arrow of magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: 魔力を矢として放つ直接干渉
findings.governingReading: Even direct interference or attack that fires magical energy as an arrow is ineffective.
findings.explanation: Intervention sounds social or procedural and fails to identify the direct magical attack being contrasted with curses.

findings.highlight: a Noble Phantasm that can even kill Saber
findings.evidenceJa: セイバーを出し抜くほどの宝具
findings.governingReading: Rider possesses a Noble Phantasm sufficient to outwit or get past Saber.
findings.explanation: The English invents the much stronger demonstrated capacity to kill Saber.

findings.highlight: use the weapon she uses
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァントが使ってる武器を借りて
findings.governingReading: A human could borrow a weapon used by a Servant and attack Saber in her sleep.
findings.explanation: The English’s she points to Saber and narrows the example into borrowing her own weapon, altering the proposed means.

findings.highlight: in spirit form like them
findings.evidenceJa: サーヴァント自身と同じ霊格
findings.governingReading: A Servant’s weapon has the same spiritual rank or order as the Servant and therefore should be able to wound one.
findings.explanation: Spirit form substitutes material state for spiritual rank and breaks Rin’s causal explanation.

findings.highlight: or something that has an effect on the Noble Phantasm itself
findings.evidenceJa: 宝具そのものに効果がある物
findings.governingReading: Saber supposes it is an automatic armament independent of Rider’s skill or magical energy, one whose efficacy lies in the Noble Phantasm itself.
findings.explanation: Or turns an appositional explanation into a second alternative and makes it sound as though the weapon affects a Noble Phantasm.

findings.highlight: Saber comments to Tohsaka
findings.evidenceJa: なんとも言えない顔つきで相づちをうつセイバー
findings.governingReading: Saber responds with an indescribable expression while beginning to compare her own Noble Phantasm.
findings.explanation: The English removes the facial cue that exposes her unknightly competitive feeling before she admits it.

findings.highlight: weapons to defeat people
findings.evidenceJa: 人を倒す
findings.governingReading: Invisible Air and Gae Bolg are armaments whose use remains directed at defeating a person.
findings.explanation: Other beings broadens the target beyond people and weakens the technical basis of the anti-person classification.

findings.highlight: specialized against others
findings.evidenceJa: 対人に優れたもの
findings.governingReading: Rin recalls Noble Phantasms specialized against individuals and those specialized against armies.
findings.explanation: Others fails to preserve the person-versus-army classification.

findings.highlight: Rider’s Noble Phantasm is powerful, but it’s not a continuous Noble Phantasm
findings.evidenceJa: その分使用にかなりの制限があるんじゃないかしら
findings.governingReading: Rin hypothesizes that Rider’s powerful Noble Phantasm probably carries substantial restrictions on use.
findings.explanation: The English omits the inference that motivates the gun-and-missile analogy and the plan to survive or preempt its limited use.

findings.highlight: it’ll be blown away before she could swing it
findings.evidenceJa: 剣を振るう前に吹き飛ばされる
findings.governingReading: Shirou fears Saber will be blown away before she can swing even her impressive invisible sword.
findings.explanation: The pronoun makes the sword the object blown away, changing the imagined victim and combat result.

findings.highlight: We don’t know what Rider’s Noble Phantasm is, and additionally, it is too powerful.
findings.evidenceJa: ライダーの宝具が何か判らない上、その威力は絶大すぎる
findings.governingReading: The active Japanese moves from “that is the conclusion” directly to the absence of a countermeasure; this explanatory sentence is commented out.
findings.explanation: mirror moon restores superseded narration and redundantly hardens the discussion’s provisional assessment.
